text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps other developers work with it. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions. Use clear and meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is maintainable, meaning it is simple to update or fix later. When you write readable code with good names and small functions, you save time for yourself and your team in the long run.
